A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same romanized language-identification study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original fastText and mT5 experiments on Bhasha-Abhijnaanam and Dakshina, including training-data ablations, sensitivity analyses, and classification errors.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds an empirical analysis of generated spelling variation in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions use pair n-gram transliteration models, 1-best or top-8 sampled romanizations, combined training corpora, and fastText/mT5 classifiers. V2 specifies global Viterbi extraction and temperature-1 sampling more explicitly; this documents the existing procedure rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The 20-language B-A task, eleven-language Dakshina development coverage, romanization lexicons, and MADLAD/GlotCC training sources are retained. The new spelling analysis examines existing synthetic data without introducing another dataset, domain, or LID test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain fastText, mT5-base, mT5-large, the published IndicLID baselines, and the same training-data alternatives. The added linguistic references do not introduce evaluated LID comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a diagnostic protocol comparing 1-best and sampled tokens through Levenshtein edits and coding 200 frequent character-edit patterns across ten displayed languages. Existing LID splits, training settings, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Accuracy is omitted from main development tables but explicitly remains computed.

E4.justification: V1 analyzes training-data choices, data quantities, and classification errors but does not directly audit the generated spelling patterns. V2 adds a substantial mechanism-focused analysis in Section 4.7 and Appendix D, with token comparisons, linguistic categorization, and extensive examples testing whether sampling produces recognizable natural romanization variation.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same five-run averaging procedure for harvested-data experiments. V2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, seed disclosures, or changed uncertainty practices; the new spelling-pattern counts are descriptive results.

E6.justification: V2 adds diagnostic findings: 31% of generated tokens differ between sampling and 1-best decoding, while 49% of the 200 selected edit patterns concern vowel length/quality and 25.5% concern implicit vowels. Tables 4–8 remove accuracy entries while retaining their F1 values. Matched benchmark scores, existing plotted results, and classification-error counts remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. V2's expanded inference explanation and descriptive spelling categories do not add or revise formal mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract's performance claims and the central contributions concerning sampled synthetic data and lightweight classifiers remain unchanged. V2's introduction additionally identifies analysis of the generated spelling variation as a contribution, modestly extending the stated contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 develops the mechanism explanation by connecting generated edits to implicit vowels, vowel length/quality, aspiration, gemination, and other linguistic phenomena. This refines the existing claim that sampling captures natural variation. The stated applicability limits concerning language coverage, closed-class classification, and alternative scripts are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a replication-resource repository pointer, dataset/model access and licensing information, and details about global top-8 inference, temperature 1, and Nisaba utilities. Appendix A newly reports 164.3 TensorCore-hours on Cloud TPU v3 for mT5-large and CPU training times of minutes for fastText. These are documentation additions, with existing training hyperparameters retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references supporting the linguistic analysis, including Demirsahin et al. (2022), Schiffman (1999), and Bhatia (2010). It also expands background on parallel romanization resources and GlotLID's efficiency motivation. The broader positioning relative to previous LID research remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and several explanatory passages, adds a results roadmap and acknowledgements, and moves the oversampling description into Section 3.1. A new Appendix D shifts the former appendices D and E to E and F. These are localized expansions and organizational refinements within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: V2 simplifies Tables 4–8 to F1-only displays, adds spelling-analysis Tables 12–13, and reorganizes the former Table 12 into Table 14 with side-by-side columns for including or excluding B-A data. Existing figures retain their plotted content, while tables and surrounding text are reflowed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility documentation and adds a linguistic audit of synthetic variation that v1 lacked, strengthening the explanation behind unchanged benchmark findings. The gain is limited: the new percentages describe selected edit-pattern types, although Section 4.7 calls them instances, and do not directly establish agreement with human variation frequencies. Overall, the added explanatory support and implementation clarity outweigh these localized weaknesses.
